stem_bark.text: The bark of Grewia flavescens is grey-brownish coloured. The main stem of the shrub is 4-angled and deeply grooved.
stem_bark.text_html:
The bark of Grewia flavescens is grey-brownish coloured.
The main stem of the shrub is 4-angled and deeply grooved.

seed.text: The seed of Grewia flavescens is enclosed into a stone. The stone is globose, very hard, with an irregular surface. It is about 5 mm across and there is 1 stone per fruit.

fruit.text: The fruit of Grewia flavescens is a drupe, brown coloured when ripe. This fruit is globose (sometimes 2-lobbed), about 1 cm across and stellate tomentose. The epicarp (fruit-wall) is crustaceous and the mesocarp (pulp) is fibrous. The fruit is 1- or 2-seeded.
fruit.text_html:
The fruit of Grewia flavescens is a drupe, brown coloured when ripe.

The epicarp (fruit-wall) is crustaceous and the mesocarp (pulp) is fibrous.

flower.text: The flowers of Grewia flavescens are bright yellow, 1.5-2 cm across and they are grouped in axillary 3-flowered clusters (cymes). The peduncle is about 5-6 mm long covered with long hairs. The bracts are ovate, 4 cm long and 3 mm wide with an acute apex. The calyx is composed of 5 sepals . They are linear, 1.5 cm long and 0.25 cm wide, bright yellow above and greenish stellate-tomentose beneath. They curve back when the flower is in full bloom. The corolla is composed of 5 bright yellow petals , hairy only at the base. They are linear, 1.5 cm long and 2 mm wide with a bifid tip. The yellow stamens are numerous with 8-12 mm long filiform filaments and tiny versatile anthers. The ovary is globose and 2-celled. The style is 12 mm long with a trifid and pointed stigma. The flower is fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Grewia flavescens are simple and distichous-arranged on the twigs. They are oblong-lanceolate, thick, stellate-tomentose and dark-green above and pale green coloured beneath. The leaves are 6-10 cm long and 2.5-3.5 cm wide with a short petiole (4-5 mm long). The apex is acute, the base is rounded to truncate and the margins are serrate. The venation is reticulate with prominent nerves.

habit.text: Grewia flavescens is a deciduous , densely branched and multi-stemmed shrub up to 4-5 meters.
habit.text_html: Grewia flavescens is a deciduous, densely branched and multi-stemmed shrub up to 4-5 meters.

ecology.text_html:
• Ecology :
    Grewia flavescens is found in open woodland, scrub jungles, thickets, on rocky hillsides, along river banks and at margins of forests; from coastal plains to 900-1000 meters of elevation.

distribution.text_html:
• Distribution :
    Grewia flavescens is distributed throughout tropical Africa, Arabian Peninsula and India.

reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :
    Bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).
  • Mode of pollination :
    Grewia flavescens is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.
  • Seed dispersal :
    The seeds of Grewia flavescens are mainly dispersed by various frugivorous birds and mammals.

medicinal.text: The fruit of Grewia flavescens contains remarkably high amounts of iron. ( Nutritional composition of Grewia species fruits, G.O. Mohammed Elhassan and S.M. Yagi, 2010 ) That supports the traditional use of the plant in the treatment of anemia.

reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :
    Grewia flavescens grows in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining and the plant prefers open lands with full sun.
    Grewia flavescens can be grown from seed but germination is unpredictable. The stones that have passed through the stomach of wild fruit-eaters germinate rapidly (stomach acids dissolve the tough stone coat).
  • Seed treatments :
    12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
